main_body: Round leaf canopy made of several lobed clumps, on a brown trunk with a flared root base
top_band: Canopy clumps have lighter green dome tops (rows ~3-12 per lobe) that shade to dark green on the lower parts; the trunk has no top surface. It reads as a volumetric organic form, not a flat elevation.
evidence: The canopy is built from overlapping round lobes. Each lobe has a light top highlight and darker lower, shadowed underside, with dark shadow rows beneath each clump (rows ~25, ~39, ~53). This reads as a top-lit volume seen from a high angle, as in the Beodeul trees. The trunk is a plain vertical column with a flared base, which is acceptable for an organic trunk. No receding side faces are present.

style.evidence: The canopy has about 5 greens, with a light highlight on each lobe, dark undersides and scattered speckle dots, so it is not a flat fill. Weaknesses: the lobes are smooth, rounded blobs with few individual leaf clumps, unlike the Beodeul references, whose canopies are made of many small leaf clusters with a bright highlight on each. The outline is dark green-black around the canopy and near-black at the underside shadows and trunk base, so it is mixed rather than a clear dark material tone. The trunk is a fairly flat brown column with only vertical grain streaks and about 3-4 brown steps. The overall look is a smoother, simpler 'sticker' tree that is thinner than the reference.
